title: Hatchling Bio — sandbox integration scratchpad
content:
Context:
Quick personal scratchpad from intake + architecture sync with Hatchling Bio (2/14). They want a lightweight sandbox deployment to validate LLM-driven lab-result summarization and triage flows before committing to a Private deployment. Mostly notes to self — messy, will clean for handoff to Marco.

Participants:
- Dr. Elena Márquez (Hatchling product lead)
- Rajiv Suresh (Hatchling infra)
- Marco Ruiz (R-INF SE)
- Me (Ava)
- Samira (solutions PM, joined last 20 mins)

High-level ask:
- Provide a short-lived, low-friction sandbox that mirrors their on-prem constraints: no PHI leaves VPC, ability to call internal lab API (REST), streaming partial summaries, and structured JSON outputs for EHR ingestion. Expected demo in 3 weeks.

Non-functional targets they mentioned:
- Latency: p95 end-to-end < 200ms for single-record summarization (ideal).
- Throughput: baseline 20-30 req/s during demo; peak bursts up to 60/s tolerated for short periods.
- Context window: up to 8k tokens (lab history + notes).
- Security: Must integrate with customer KMS and log audit events to their Splunk instance.

Key technical constraints / gotchas:
1) Data residency: All payloads must stay in their VPC. That rules out hosted API for the sandbox; Private with local control plane recommended. For an initial proof, we can run a Private control plane in our cloud but with strict VPC peering and egress block — but legal prefers a customer-run control plane.
2) Auth to lab API: they have mTLS + client cert rotation every 7 days. Need to prototype support in our connector shim (SE task). Add check for cert refresh to avoid 401s during demo.
3) Tokenization mismatch risk: their token counting in legacy code differs from our tokenizer (particularly for protein sequences and chemical formulas). Add a brief tokenization test set as part of the evaluation harness.
4) Output structure: they want function-calling-like structured outputs (diagnosis_code, severity_score, recommended_actions[]) — we should use streaming + JSON-safe function schema to avoid partial parse failures. Include an aggressive post-parse validator in the sandbox.
5) Caching semantics: Many calls will be identical across patients (standard lab interpretation). Recommend prefix-KV caching at request-level with TTL 24h; but careful with PII-free cache keys (hash of normalized lab schema).
6) Model family: for cost/latency tradeoff start with redwood-small-8k (quantized) for demo, have fallback to opt-6b or redwood-medium if quality fails. Need to prepare a short evaluation matrix.
7) Quantization / perf: client is open to int8 quantized models, but they require us to validate numeric stability on lab-value heavy inputs. Plan test vectors with edge-case ranges (e.g., blood gas extremes).
8) Streaming & partial results: their UI needs earliest partial summary (first sentence) to show perceived responsiveness. We'll wire SSE or websockets; ensure our SDK stream chunks include finalization flag so UI doesn't keep waiting.
9) Audit & logs: They need de-identified logs to ship to Splunk for monitoring; raw PHI should be redacted in transit. We'll add a pipeline step to redact known PHI patterns before export, but ensure we keep correlation ids for debugging.

Open questions to resolve (action owners in parens):
- Can Hatchling accept a temporary managed control plane with VPC peering for the initial demo, or insist on customer-managed from day 1? (Dr. Elena / Rajiv)
- What exact agent/REST endpoints do we need to call on their lab system and are there rate-limits? (Rajiv)
- Which KMS provider and what integration (AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault, on-prem HSM)? Will they provide an IAM role for us to test? (Marco / Rajiv)
- Are there compliance artifacts we should collect for legal (BAA, DPIA) ahead of POC? (Samira)

Immediate next steps (timeline + owners):
- Today (Ava): spin up a minimal Private sandbox in our staging VPC with egress blocked; create demo route with redwood-small-8k model. Short smoke test with synthetic lab payloads. (ETA: 2 business days)
- 2/17 (Marco): prototype connector shim that supports mTLS client cert rotation; add a local test service that simulates cert expiry. (ETA: 4 business days)
- 2/19 (Samira): start compliance checklist and ask legal to prioritize a short BAA template. (ETA: 3 business days)
- 2/21 (Ava + Marco): run tokenization/quantization edge-case tests (protein sequences, chemical formulas, extreme numeric ranges). Capture failure cases in GH issue.
- 2/24 (Team): internal dry-run demo for Hatchling; collect feedback and adjust canary rollout plan.

Test plan sketches (for handoff to QA):
- Inputs: 50 canonical lab records (typical), 20 edge-case numeric extremes, 15 long-history multi-entry cases (~8k tokens).
- Metrics: ROUGE-L and custom entailment checks for correctness, p95 latency, memory/kvcache hit rate, false redaction rate (for PI removal).
- Acceptance: Demo passes if 85% of typical records produce valid JSON outputs with severity in expected range and p95 latency < 350ms (we'll push to <200ms but give initial buffer).

Deployment & rollout notes:
- Canary strategy: 0% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 48 hours with automatic rollback on error rate > 3x baseline or median latency > 2x baseline. Document this for their release ops.
- Fallbacks: route to hosted-compatible model variant if local capacity is saturated. Must ensure de-identification before any host-level fallback.

Random TODOs / notes to self:
- Add tokenization unit tests to repo: tests/tokenize_hatchling.py
- Create GH issue template for quantization failures with reproducible payloads
- Remind legal to check whether Splunk ingestion endpoint requires us to use TLS mutual auth (likely)
- Prepare a simple slide (1 pager) that compares redwood-small vs opt-6b for demo: latency, cost, quality bullet points (for 2/24 dry-run)
- Check infra quota for staging gpus (n4 -> need 2x A10s for consistent perf)

Meeting notes (raw):
- Dr. Elena: "We can't have PHI leave the building — even during POC. We need to see the model explain why it flagged a triage priority."
- Rajiv: concerned about client cert rotation — "we rotate every week, so any connector has to be able to pick up new certs without restarts".
- Marco: suggested running a cert agent that watches a mounted cert file and hot-reloads the connector. Good short-term.
- I asked about evaluation metrics — they've got a clinical team willing to grade outputs but want a quick automatic gate to avoid wasting clinician time.

Draft email to Hatchling (send after staging test):
Subject: Quick follow-up + next steps for sandbox demo
Hi Elena / Rajiv,

Thanks again for the sync today. We're building the staging sandbox today and will validate a handful of synthetic lab records against redwood-small-8k. Marco will prototype the mTLS connector and Samira is starting the compliance checklist.

Action items for you: could you share a stubbed lab API endpoint (or OpenAPI spec) + a sample encrypted client cert for testing rotation? Also confirm the KMS provider so we can exercise key wrapping.

I'll ping you after the first smoke run with logs and a short recording.

Best,
Ava

-----
Notes to self: don't forget to add the sandbox route to cost-monitoring dashboard; set alerts for tokenization anomalies (we saw one weird protein token boundary in the meeting).

End of scratchpad.
